theme: Do less, get more: stop wasting effort on things that don't move results

posts.topic: Hashtags vs sends: what actually drives Instagram reach
posts.angle: Myth vs fact, citing Mosseri and the 5-hashtag cap
hook_options: 30 hashtags won't grow you. Sends will.
Instagram capped hashtags at 5. Here's why.

slides.hook_sub: What Instagram's head actually said about reach.
slides.visual: White ground, huge ExtraBold hook, 'Sends will.' in red on its own line, Swipe → footer

slides.title: More hashtags, more reach?
slides.body: Instagram now caps posts at 5 hashtags. Adam Mosseri has said hashtags don't meaningfully increase reach.
slides.visual: Grey #F3F4F6 ground, '#' symbol crossed with red line, big '5' in red

slides.title: What hashtags actually do
slides.body: They tell Instagram and searchers what your post is about. Use 3-5 specific tags, not #love #instagood.
slides.visual: Two tag chips: '#instagood' struck through, '#promptengineering' with red tick

slides.title: What drives reach instead
slides.body: Mosseri named watch time, likes and sends as the top 3 ranking signals (Jan 2025).
slides.visual: Three stacked rows: Watch time / Likes / Sends, red → before Sends

slides.title: Sends reach new people
slides.body: When someone forwards your post in a DM, it lands with people who may not follow you yet.
slides.visual: Grey ground, simple paper-plane line icon with red arrow to 3 new circles

slides.title: Make posts worth sending
slides.body: Before posting, ask: who would I forward this to? Checklists, templates and relatable truths get sent. Generic tips don't.
slides.visual: Question in quote marks, three small check items below

slides.cta_body: Insights → post → Shares. Send this to a friend still using 30 hashtags.
slides.visual: Red #DC2626 button shape with 'Send this', handle footer

posts.caption:
Hashtags don't grow your reach on Instagram. Adam Mosseri, who runs Instagram, has said so himself.

Instagram now also caps posts at 5 hashtags, so pasting 30 is over.

What hashtags still do: tell Instagram and search what your post is about.

What drives reach: Mosseri named watch time, likes and sends as the top 3 signals. Sends matter because a forwarded post reaches people who don't follow you yet.

Try this this week. Open Insights on each post and check Shares. Make more of whatever got shared most.

Send this to a friend who still uses 30 hashtags.

Instagram now caps posts at 5 hashtags, and Adam Mosseri has said hashtags don't meaningfully increase reach.

What does? In January 2025 he named the top three ranking signals: watch time, likes and sends.

For small businesses, sends are the interesting one. A forwarded post lands in front of people who don't follow you yet. That's free distribution.

A practical change for this week: stop judging posts by likes. Open each post's insights and track Shares. Make more of whatever gets forwarded.

posts.caption:
Stop collecting AI tools. Ten free trials won't make your work faster.

To start, you need 2:
1. A chat assistant (ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini) to think, write and plan
2. A design tool (like Canva) for posts and visuals

Don't add a third until these two speed up your daily work. Start free, and pay only when you actually hit the limit.

posts.topic: Answer repeat DMs in 1 tap with Instagram saved replies + ChatGPT
posts.angle: 4-step how-to for small business owners, phone only, free
hook_options: Answering the same DM daily? Do it in 1 tap.
Your DMs ask the same 5 questions.

slides.hook_sub: Instagram saved replies + ChatGPT. Free, works on your phone.
slides.visual: White ground, phone outline with chat bubble, red '1 tap'

slides.title: Price? Location? Timings?
slides.body: If your DMs keep asking the same 5-6 questions, typing each reply by hand eats your week.
slides.visual: Grey ground, 3 repeating chat bubbles with the questions

slides.title: List your top 5 DM questions
slides.body: Scroll your last 30 DMs. Write down what repeats: price, location, timings, delivery, booking.

slides.title: Draft replies with ChatGPT
slides.body: Prompt: 'Write 5 short, friendly DM replies for my [business] answering: [questions]. Under 40 words each, end with one next step.'
slides.visual: Prompt in a light grey code-style box; [brackets] in red

slides.title: Save them in Instagram
slides.body: Settings → Business tools → Saved replies → +. Add a shortcut like 'price' and paste the reply. Menu names vary by version.

slides.title: Type the shortcut, tap, send
slides.body: In any DM, type 'price' and tap the suggestion. Edit one detail so it still feels personal.
slides.visual: Chat bar mock with 'price' typed and a suggestion chip

slides.cta_body: Needs a Business or Creator account. Start with your top 3 questions.

posts.caption:
Instagram saved replies answer the same DM in 1 tap. If you type the same answers to 'price?' and 'where are you?' every day, this is a 15-minute setup.

1. Go through your last 30 DMs and list the questions that repeat
2. Ask ChatGPT for 5 short replies (prompt on slide 4)
3. Add them to Instagram's Saved replies, each with a shortcut like 'price'
4. In a DM, type the shortcut, tap, change one detail, send

One rule: when your price or timings change, update the saved reply too. A fast wrong answer is worse than a slow right one.

Needs a Business or Creator account. Menu names can differ slightly by app version.

Save this for when you set it up.

A small, free automation most local businesses skip: Instagram saved replies.

If your DMs keep asking about price, location and timings, set it up once:
1. List the 5 questions that repeat in your last 30 DMs
2. Draft short, friendly replies with ChatGPT (under 40 words, one next step each)
3. Save each one in Instagram under Saved replies with a shortcut like 'price'
4. Type the shortcut in a DM, tap, personalise one detail, send

It needs a Business or Creator account. Keep the replies updated when your prices or hours change; a fast wrong answer is worse than a slow right one.

posts.topic: Write ad copy like a WhatsApp message
posts.angle: Do/Don't contrast for local business ad copy
hook_options: Write ads like a WhatsApp message.
Your ad reads like a pamphlet.

headline_options: Write ads like a WhatsApp message | not a pamphlet
Your ad reads like a pamphlet. | Fix it.
Talk to one person. | Not to everyone.
static.headline: Write ads like a WhatsApp message
static.support: Do: talk to one person, show the ₹ price, give one next step. Don't: 'best quality', 5 offers, no price.
static.cta: Send this to someone running ads
static.visual: Split card: left 'Do' column with red ticks, right 'Don't' column in grey with strikethrough; no stock photos

posts.caption:
Write your ad copy like a WhatsApp message, not a pamphlet.

Pamphlet copy: "Best quality, lowest price, all services available, contact now!" Nobody stops for it.

WhatsApp copy: "Home AC service for ₹499, same-day visit in Jammu city. Reply 'AC' to book a slot."

The difference:
→ Talks to one person
→ Shows the ₹ price
→ Gives one next step

Before your next ad, read it out loud. If you wouldn't send it to a friend, don't send it to a customer.

Send this to a friend who runs ads for their shop.
